questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and go slowly.
Look left and right to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that are stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left and right to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: At places where people may cross or traffic meets, look to the left and right sides of your vehicle. Make sure no one is coming before you proceed.

questions.question: A large truck ahead of you is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. The truck:

options.text: May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: The rear wheels of a vehicle follow a shorter path than the front wheels when turning. Long trucks need extra space to turn right, so they often swing wide.

questions.question: For drivers 21 years old or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
0.02 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: Drivers age 21 or older cannot drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Yield the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
Yield the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down and go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Give the right-of-way to any traffic that is close enough to be a problem.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
Keep more distance between your vehicle and the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep more distance between your vehicle and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because it is darker. You cannot see as well or judge distances as easily. Keep more distance between you and the car ahead in case it stops suddenly. Use your headlights correctly by switching between high and low beams as needed.

questions.question: If a tire blows out, you should:

options.text: Press the brake hard and hold it.
Hold the steering wheel tightly and brake gently.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tightly and brake gently.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel tightly to keep the vehicle straight. Take your foot off the gas and brake gently. Slow down gradually. Pull off the road in a safe place when you can.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. You should:

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your front wheels left to be ready to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Signal about 100 feet before making a left turn. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This prevents another vehicle from pushing you into oncoming traffic if it hits you from behind.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
Keep more distance between your vehicle and the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep more distance between your vehicle and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: Keep more distance between you and other cars when it is dark and hard to see. Use your headlights and follow the rules for high beams and low beams. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights, as the glare can blind you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down; curving road ahead.
Slow down and do not use your brakes.
Slow down; road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down; road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: If another car is following you too closely on a two-lane road:

options.text: Slowly reduce your speed so the other car will drive around you.
Speed up to increase the distance between the cars.
Brake to slow down, then go back to your original speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly reduce your speed so the other car will drive around you.
questions.explanation: If a car is following too closely, try to change lanes if possible. If you cannot change lanes, slowly reduce your speed when the road ahead is clear. This will encourage the other driver to pass you.

questions.question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, what can they do?

options.text: They may use the left lane.
They may cut through all lanes.
They may wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride with traffic on the road. You should expect to see a bicyclist using the left lane when turning left.

questions.question: If your car begins to skid out of control, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes lightly.
Stay off the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, do not use the brakes. Keep steering to regain control until the vehicle moves safely down the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
Slippery when wet.
Road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about dangers ahead. This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what must you do?

options.text: Must yield the right-of-way to traffic close enough to cause a collision.
Must yield to vehicles only on your right.
Should slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must yield the right-of-way to traffic close enough to cause a collision.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, give the right-of-way to traffic in the lanes you plan to enter or cross. Be ready to stop, but you can go if there is no conflicting traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge right.
Divided highway begins.
Lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane is ending ahead. Drivers in that lane must merge into another lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Falling rocks
Trucks use second gear
Steep hill

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that a steep hill is ahead. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: If heavy smoke covers the road ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your flashers and continue.
Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the road.
Turn on your high beams and continue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: If heavy smoke covers the road, slow down right away. Move as far right as you can and stop off the road. Then check if it is safe to continue. Some smoke can harm your eyes, lungs, or be deadly.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow light at an intersection and have not entered yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Slow down and proceed carefully through the intersection.
Come to a safe stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a safe stop.
questions.explanation: At a steady yellow light, stop safely if you have not entered the intersection. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through safely.

questions.question: What color are regulatory signs?

options.text: Green.
Yellow.
White.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers about traffic laws they must follow. These laws are about direction, lanes, turns, speed, parking, or special situations. Regulatory signs are usually white squares or rectangles with black, red, or green text or symbols.

questions.question: You park facing uphill on a street with a curb. After setting the brake, what should you do with the front wheels?

options.text: Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Leave the front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb. When parking uphill without a curb or parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or edge of the road.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:

options.text: In a marked crosswalk.
In any crosswalk or intersection.
Crossing any street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing any street.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians crossing the street anywhere. This includes marked and unmarked crosswalks. Always give pedestrians the right-of-way for safety.

questions.question: When the road is wet and slippery after rain starts, you should:

options.text: Avoid making turns and stops while driving at high speeds.
Test your tires' grip while going uphill.
Look less far ahead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making turns and stops while driving at high speeds.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire grip. Drive slowly to prevent skidding. Avoid fast turns or sudden stops on wet pavement.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?

options.text: Service sign.
Regulatory sign.
Warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. Examples include curve warnings, steep grade warnings, or other dangerous conditions.

questions.question: If you are under 21, your license can be suspended if you drive with a blood alcohol level of:

options.text: 0.15 percent or more.
0.08 percent or more.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: There is zero tolerance for alcohol if you are under 21. Any amount of alcohol will result in penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: You want to park uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels toward the side of the road. This way, if your brakes fail, the car rolls away from traffic, not into it.

questions.question: Broken yellow lines separate:

options.text: Lanes where no passing is allowed.
Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can pass on the left when it is safe.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle on the right shoulder:

options.text: If the shoulder is paved.
When the car in front of you is driving too slowly.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You cannot drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle. Never leave the pavement to pass.

questions.question: When should you use your high beam headlights?

options.text: Within 500 feet of another vehicle
In busy traffic
On open country roads

questions.correctAnswerText: On open country roads
questions.explanation: Use high beams only on open country roads when no other cars are nearby. Always drive slower at night.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with a siren and flashing lights is approaching while you are in an intersection. You should:

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.
questions.explanation: Finish crossing the intersection, then move to the right and stop. Always yield to emergency vehicles using lights or sirens.

questions.question: A broken yellow centerline means:

options.text: Passing is not permitted.
Passing on the right is allowed when the road is clear.
Passing on the left is allowed when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing on the left is allowed when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass on the left if there is no oncoming traffic. Never cross a solid yellow line to pass.
